newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MACK RETURNS FROM JAPAN TO JOIN RED SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MACK RETURNS FROM JAPAN TO JOIN RED SOX.

text.p: Shane Mack is back in the major leagues, signing on with the Boston Red Sox after a two-year stint in Japan.
The Red Sox agreed to terms Saturday with Mack on a contract for the 1997 season.

The 33-year-old Mack played two seasons with the Yomiuri Giants of the Japanese League after a five-year stretch with the Minnesota Twins. He averaged a .300 batting mark, 20 homers and 80 RBI in Japan.

"Shane Mack will bring many dimensions to the Red Sox ballclub," said Boston general manager Dan Duquette. "He has strong athletic ability, great speed, excellent defensive instincts and skill, and a proven bat."
During his tenure with the Twins from 1990 to 1994, Mack hit .309 with 67 home runs, 315 RBI and 71 stolen bases in 633 games.
Mack began his career with the San Diego Padres in 1987 and 1988. In seven major league seasons, he has a career .299 average.
